newsitem.title: UK: Bildt urges Serbia's Milosevic to show restraint.
newsitem.headline: Bildt urges Serbia's Milosevic to show restraint.

text.p: Carl Bildt, the international High Representative to Bosnia, on Saturday called on Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to recognise the findings of an OSCE mission and exercise restraint towards demonstrators.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said on Friday that the opposition coalition had won disputed local elections in November. Milosevic's decision to ignore the results has sparked large anti-government demonstrations.
"I would urge President Milosevic to recognise the findings of the OSCE Mission led by Mr (Felipe) Gonzalez," Bildt said in a statement issued in London through his spokesman Michael Maclay.

"I call upon the authorities in Belgrade to exercise the greatest restraint in connection with the demonstrations which continue in peace and dignity day by day, and I am deeply disturbed by the reports of violence in reaction to these demonstrations in recent days," Bildt said.

Vuk Draskovic, leader of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition, has urged its supporters to attend the funeral of Predrag Starcevic who was apparently trampled to death in a stampede during a demonstration on Tuesday.
Bildt ended his statement by saying "the development of democracy in Serbia is of crucial importance for peace and stability throughout the region".
